_comment: The labels I wrote by hand for the doctl answer key.
Why this file exists. The maintainers' labels cover 304 of 536 issues and lean
hard one way: 159 bug, 99 enhancement, 26 security (all bot-written CVE
reports), 15 question, about 5 documentation. An answer key built only from
those would have almost no documentation or 'other' examples, so there would be
no way to measure how well a model finds them, and a six-category test would
quietly be a two-category test.
So these are hand labels for a spread of the 232 issues that carry no useful
maintainer label. It leans towards documentation, question and other on
purpose, and it also includes a deliberate block of bug and enhancement items,
so that 'I labelled it' and 'the category is rare' aren't the same set of
issues.
These win where they overlap with the automatic mapping. Where the maintainers
had a view too and it differs, the disagreement is recorded and reported rather
than quietly overwritten.
Every label below came from reading the title and body against the rules in
ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md. Issues I judged genuinely ambiguous are listed under
'excluded' with a reason, instead of being forced into a category. Forcing them
would add noise that punishes whichever model happened to read them the other
way.
